items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: I had Tom Johnson in the band from here. I just hired Tom... Tom Johnson was playing trumpet.

ctx.x: What about Thomasville? Do you mind talking about that?

No, no. The reason for that is I had Tom Johnson in the band from here. I just hired Tom and I had a boy named Buddy Collins, who was a singer. And he started a fight in the auditorium that night of free-for-all. And I was on the front door with the principal of the school, taking care of the business and the money. They hurdled a whole band off in a paddy wagon, two girls I had that were dancers, the James sisters. Put them all in there. Of course, a few of the fellas got away. Mickey and I think it was Kato and…
The demand wasn't involved in the fight or anything?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: And then Tom Johnson was a saxophone player. And I got through some of my old men back. They wanted to come back in the band.

ctx.x: He is. He's a preacher. No kidding. And then Tom Johnson was a saxophone player. And I got through some of my old men back. They wanted to come back in the band. But it didn't last. I had to pick it up again after this guy messed the beans out of his money. And I said, well I'm into it again. I better just go ahead and go to book it again. So I went to book the band again. That's another one of those unfortunate situations that came up. I didn't know I just said. Oh the clock is making them out. I see.
I just wanted to tell you. Did you ever know Nat Tolles? Nat did one of the greatest, which I played with Nat in New Orleans at the theater,
